kjv: the giants, the sons of Anak, [which come] of the giants
mine: the Nephilim (the sons of Anak are from the Nephilim)
note: Hebrew nephilim is a proper term (cf. Gen 6:4) of uncertain meaning; the KJV follows the Septuagint gigantes. The parenthesis linking Anakim to Nephilim is part of the spies' exaggeration. Context: the Nephilim, seen as giants (medium confidence). Nephilim is a proper term (Gen 6:4) of uncertain meaning; transliterating it, as ESV, NIV, NASB, NRSV, NJPS and CSB do, keeps it open, while the grasshopper comparison shows the spies meant men of huge size. The parenthesis linking Anakim to Nephilim is absent from the LXX and may be a gloss. Other possible meanings: (1) 'giants' — LXX and Vulgate gigantes, KJV; (2) 'fallen ones', from naphal 'fall' — some Jewish interpreters (cf. Rashi on Gen 6:4); (3) the parenthesis as a later scribal note rather than part of the spies' speech — many commentators, since the LXX lacks it.
